jobs.state_note: MAJOR FINDING: Job 287064 (7-script set, XTPlot fully removed) OOM-killed (TERM_EXTERNAL_SIGNAL) at Max Memory 935GB -- nearly DOUBLE the ~455-457GB ceiling seen in every prior attempt this session, and ran 917s (longer than any previous attempt, which died at 392-591s). converge.log never advanced past mesh-setup/Catalyst-init the whole time (stalled at 20616 bytes/mtime 16:33:55). This breaks the 'fixed content-independent ceiling' theory: fewer scripts + longer runtime + no XTPlot still produced a HIGHER peak memory than heavier configs. New leading hypothesis: memory usage grows continuously with wall-clock time (a genuine leak in CONVERGE's Catalyst/pvbatch stack, not tied to specific script content), and the actual OOM point depends on how much free RAM the shared ttc node happens to have available at that moment (other users' jobs on the same node could explain the 455GB vs 935GB variance between runs). This significantly complicates the diagnosis -- worth considering: (a) does the node have other tenants/shared memory contention, (b) is there a genuine unbounded leak in the pvbatch/Catalyst driver itself independent of scripts, (c) multi-node LSF ttcmult may still be the most robust path forward regardless of root cause.
